Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I've been farming this land for 50 years — my father farmed it before me. I know every corner of these 11.6 mu.

---

**How I split the land this year**

Same as last year, more or less. Cotton is still my main cash crop — I put about 6 mu in cotton on the sandier field on the west side, that ground has always done better for cotton than wheat. Then I've got about 4 mu of good flat land where I do wheat-maize double crop, that's my food and a bit of extra grain to sell. I keep about 1 mu of millet for the family — my wife likes to cook it, and it handles dry years when the wheat doesn't. And a small patch, maybe 6 fen (0.6 mu), of mungbean — it's good for the soil, and the daughter-in-law takes some when she visits from town.

**Cotton (6 mu) — the one that pays the bills**

I plant around April 20, after the soil warms up. I buy hybrid cotton seed from the agricultural supply shop in town, the same brand the successful farmers in the village use — costs about 60 yuan per mu but worth it, the local saved seed doesn't yield like it used to. Before planting I put down about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu, then at squaring stage I topdress 15 kg of urea — so that's about 12 kg of N per mu total. The extension guy at the township office keeps telling us to use less N, but cotton likes nitrogen and I don't want yellow plants.

Cotton is work. I'll irrigate twice from the well — once before flowering if it's dry, and once during boll-filling. That well water isn't cheap, the electricity meter spins. Pesticide? Cotton needs it, no way around it. Bollworm, aphids, spider mites — I spray maybe 4-5 times through the season. My hands aren't as steady as they were, so my son helps when he can get off work. Picking starts in September and we're at it through October — I hire two or three women from the village for the picking, pay them by the day.

I'm hoping for around 250 kg of lint per mu. Last year I got 240, the year before 260. Depends on weather.

**Wheat (4 mu) — planted last October, harvesting in June**

The wheat is already in the ground from last October. I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting. Before the spring green-up I'll topdress around 15 kg of urea per mu — the extension leaflet said 12 is enough but my soil is tired, 15 is what works for me. Total N is maybe 17-18 kg per mu.

Three irrigations planned: one in early spring at green-up, one at jointing, one at heading. If it rains well in April I'll skip the heading one and save the electricity. I spray once for aphids usually, and a weed spray in early spring. Expecting 450 kg per mu if the weather is decent.

**Maize (4 mu) — right after wheat**

Soon as we combine the wheat in mid-June, we have maybe 5 days to get the maize in. No time to plow properly — we use the no-till planter that the village cooperative rents out, it drills the maize right into the wheat stubble. Hybrid seed, about 60 yuan per mu. I put base fertilizer with the seed — another 40 kg of compound — and then at the big bell stage (around July 20) I topdress urea, maybe 15 kg. So about 15 kg N per mu.

Maize usually doesn't need much irrigation if the summer rains come. If it's dry at silking, I'll irrigate once. That's it. Spray once for corn borer. Hoping for 500 kg per mu.

**Millet (1 mu) — for the house**

Plant in late May on a small patch near the house. I save seed from last year — no point buying for millet. Put a little compound fertilizer, maybe 20 kg total on the whole mu. No irrigation, millet handles dry. No pesticide. My wife and I harvest it by hand in September, dry it on the flat roof. Maybe 200 kg for the family. That's food, not money.

**Mungbean (0.6 mu) — for the soil and the family**

Plant early June in a corner where I had maize the year before. Barely any fertilizer — mungbean fixes its own nitrogen, and that's actually part of why I grow it, the field does better the year after. Maybe 5 kg of urea at planting, that's it. No irrigation, no pesticide. Harvest in August by hand. Gets us maybe 50 kg of beans.

---

**What I'm worried about**

Fertilizer prices went up again this year, I'm hearing urea is 15% more than last spring. I've already budgeted for the amounts I wrote above — if prices keep climbing I might cut back on the wheat topdressing by a few kg. The cotton I won't cut, too much risk. Also the village well committee was talking about raising the electricity charge for irrigation — if that happens, I'll irrigate once less on the wheat.

Labor is the other thing. My son is in Handan working in a factory, he comes back for the busy weeks. My wife and I can do most of the daily work but picking cotton and harvesting wheat needs hired hands. I'm 65, I can't climb the ladder to fix the irrigation pipe like I used to.
